excerpts.author: lucassaldanhaconsensys
excerpts.content:
So whenever I run Teku with only EthereumJS or only Geth. Everything works fine. When I run a network with them both, right after any execution request is created (either deposits, withdrawals or consolidations), there is a fork in the network. ~~My guess is that the commitment hash calculation is wrong in one of the two.~~ Or Teku is doing something funny? 🤔 

Here is a Kurtosis config to replicate:
```
participants_matrix:
  el:
    - el_type: geth
      el_image: ethpandaops/geth:lightclient-prague-devnet-4-e100dcf
    - el_type: ethereumjs
      el_image: ethpandaops/ethereumjs:7702-devnet-4-plus-t8ntool-3f3a3cc
  cl:
    - cl_type: teku
      cl_image: ethpandaops/teku:master-b50adc4
network_params:
  electra_fork_epoch: 1
  min_validator_withdrawability_delay: 1
  shard_committee_period: 1
  churn_limit_quotient: 16
  num_validator_keys_per_node: 64
additional_services:
  - dora
  - apache
  - assertoor
dora_params:
  image: "ethpandaops/dora:pk910-electra-devnet4"
snooper_enabled: true
assertoor_params:
  run_stability_check: false
  run_block_proposal_check: false
  tests:
    - { file: "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethpandaops/assertoor/refs/heads/electra-support/playbooks/pectra-dev/all.yaml"}
```

excerpts.author: lucassaldanhaconsensys
excerpts.content:
Nethermind block production stops working upon Electra activation. They are sending the wrong `executionRequests` object when empty in `execution_getPayloadV4`:

They are sending:
```
"executionRequests": []
```
Instead of:
```
"executionRequests": [
  "0x",
  "0x",
  "0x"
]
```

Snooper logs: https://gist.github.com/lucassaldanha/fd758b166000622d7878e00c670f987e
